title: The narratives that divide us and bring us together: Neural and behavioral synchrony amongst members of historical victim and perpetrator groups
summary: Social neuroscience focuses on studying neural and behavioral synchrony in social interactions. Research applying this approach has revealed that such synchrony is crucial for mutual empathy and cooperation. The proposed research will apply these insights to the context of intergroup reconciliation. Focusing on German-Jewish relations, we aim to shed light on how the neural activity of members of historical perpetrator and victim groups diverges in response to naturalistic stimuli related to the historic transgression and whether identity-affirmation interventions previously found to increase conciliatory inclinations by addressing specific aspects of a group’s narrative can increase neural as well as behavioral and physiological synchrony across group lines. These studies will, therefore, pioneer the examination of the role of neural, physiological and behavioral synchrony in intergroup reconciliation processes.
conditions: In this study healthy control participants will be investigated.

interventions.name:
In a first study healthy control participants from Germany and Israel undergo functional magnetic resonance imaging to investigate neural synchrony, i.e. similarities in neural activity across participants from different participant groups.
